nodes.label: Layered Architecture (routes -> controllers -> services -> db)
nodes.rationale: One-directional layering: only services touch the DB; controllers stay thin glue; validation happens at the route boundary via zValidator.

nodes.label: JSON Response Envelope ({success, data} / {success, error})
nodes.rationale: All endpoints must keep a consistent JSON shape via success/error helpers in src/utils/response.js.

nodes.label: parseDbError (Postgres error code mapping)
nodes.rationale: Maps raw Postgres error codes (23505 unique, 23503 FK, 23502 not-null) to human-readable Errors so controllers can surface useful .message values.

nodes.label: New Resource Convention (schema -> validator -> service -> controller -> route)
nodes.source_location: ### Conventions to follow when adding a new resource
nodes.norm_label: new resource convention (schema -> validator -> service -> controller -> route)

nodes.label: README Quickstart (bun install / bun run dev)
nodes.norm_label: readme quickstart (bun install / bun run dev)

nodes.label: AppError (base error with .status)
nodes.rationale: A DB query that finds no row does not throw, so without a status-carrying error the controller would return 200 for missing data; AppError carries .status (default 400) so controllers can return the correct HTTP status. New subclasses are only created when a status is reused across many services or instanceof checks are needed elsewhere.

nodes.label: Controller status propagation (err.status ?? 400)
nodes.rationale: Controllers pass err.status ?? 400 to error(); errors from parseDbError have no .status and deliberately fall back to 400.

nodes.label: Error-handling YAGNI deferrals (ConflictError 409, UUID param validation)
nodes.source_location: ## Kandidat lain yang sengaja belum dibikin (YAGNI)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately not built yet: ConflictError (409) until 23505 duplicates need a distinct status, and zValidator('param') UUID checks until endpoints are publicly exposed; parseDbError currently returns plain Error for 23505 so it falls to the 400 default.
nodes.norm_label: error-handling yagni deferrals (conflicterror 409, uuid param validation)

nodes.label: Auth Schema Design (spec)
nodes.rationale: Schema-only change for password login + DB-backed session tokens using native Bun/Postgres/JS features, explicitly avoiding new auth dependencies (bcrypt/JWT libs); register/login/logout endpoints are out of scope.

nodes.label: usersTable auth columns (password, role)
nodes.rationale: password stores a hash (Bun.password.hash/verify, native bcrypt in Bun runtime, no new dependency); role uses a Postgres enum so values are constrained at the DB level rather than only in Zod.

nodes.label: sessionsTable (DB-backed session tokens)
nodes.rationale: token generated with crypto.randomUUID() (native Web Crypto) to avoid a JWT/session library; userId FK uses onDelete cascade so sessions are auto-removed when a user is deleted, avoiding manual cleanup in the service layer.

nodes.label: Auth schema YAGNI deferrals (createdAt/userAgent/ipAddress, emailVerified, auth endpoints)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately deferred until real need: session audit columns (createdAt/userAgent/ipAddress) until a 'manage login devices' feature exists, emailVerified until an email verification flow exists, and register/login/logout endpoints which are outside this schema change's scope. Written explicitly (consistent with docs/error-handling.md) so deferrals are tracked, not silently forgotten.
nodes.norm_label: auth schema yagni deferrals (createdat/useragent/ipaddress, emailverified, auth endpoints)

nodes.label: Auth Schema Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Three tasks: edit src/db/schema.database.js, generate migration with drizzle-kit, apply and verify against local Postgres. No new packages; hashing/token generation stay native (Bun.password, crypto.randomUUID) and are out of scope; verification uses drizzle-kit output and direct DB inspection because the repo has no test suite.
